title: UniLLM: A Unified Large Language Model for Multi‐Modal Urban Dynamics Prediction

problem.claim: Urban dynamics prediction requires information from multiple interrelated data sources because urban signals influence one another across modalities.

gap.claim: Existing methods are limited by single-modality focus, rigid model designs, and insufficient attention to inter-modal dependencies, reducing adaptability and predictive performance.

contributions.claim: UniLLM is a unified large language model for multi-modal urban dynamics prediction.

The Unified Cross-Modal Alignment Module transforms heterogeneous urban data into latent representations while preserving modality-specific patterns and capturing cross-modal correlations with contrastive learning.

The Routing-Aware Prompting Mechanism learns soft prompts from task context and modality semantics, while the Multi-Modal Memory-Guided Adaptive Algorithm uses replay-based gradient coordination and Frank–Wolfe optimization to mitigate cross-modal catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments across multiple cities and urban modalities show UniLLM consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors characterize UniLLM as a potentially flexible and robust forecasting model for real-world multi-modal urban environments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cities produce large amounts of urban dynamics data, whose value depends on integrating interdependent modalities.
Single urban dynamics predictions require information from multiple related sources, but existing approaches have limited scope and overlook cross-modal dependencies.
These limitations hinder adaptation to changing urban conditions and degrade predictive performance across modalities.
UniLLM combines cross-modal alignment, routing-aware prompting, and memory-guided adaptive fine-tuning.
The authors report consistent outperformance of state-of-the-art baselines across multiple cities and urban modalities and describe potential real-world flexibility and robustness.

source_observation.claim: Urban signals are interdependent, and predicting one dynamic may require multiple modalities.

interpretation.claim: Models for related urban forecasting tasks may benefit from explicitly representing cross-modal relationships.

application.claim: Consider unified representations and adaptation mechanisms when forecasting multiple interrelated urban dynamics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether cross-modal integration is beneficial for every urban forecasting task or modality.

source_observation.claim: The authors report that replay-based gradient coordination and Frank–Wolfe optimization mitigate cross-modal catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning.

interpretation.claim: Continual or multi-task fine-tuning may require mechanisms that coordinate updates across modalities.

application.claim: Evaluate memory-guided update coordination when adapting a shared forecasting model across tasks and modalities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the forgetting measurements, adaptation settings, or conditions under which this mechanism is effective.

unknowns: The specific cities, modalities, datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
The abstract does not report ablations, computational costs, failure cases, or deployment details.
